summary: Verified Scholar's Trial global leaderboard (backend + frontend) and biome route rendering. Found and fixed one CRITICAL backend bug: POST /api/leaderboard was returning HTTP 500 because Mongo's insert_one mutates the inserted dict with an ObjectId _id, which then failed FastAPI's JSON serialization. After fix, all 10 backend tests pass and frontend auto-submission from Singleplayer game-over works end-to-end.
action_items: (Optional, not blocking) Singleplayer.jsx uses getPlayerName() from lib/storage which fell through to 'Anonymous Scholar' in our test even after we set localStorage['player.name']. Confirm the storage key naming so user-set player names actually attach to their leaderboard entries instead of always submitting as 'Anonymous Scholar'.
critical_code_review_comments: FIXED: server.py submit_leaderboard mutated `doc` via insert_one which adds _id (ObjectId). FastAPI's jsonable_encoder then choked on ObjectId. Added `doc.pop('_id', None)` before returning. Standard MongoDB ObjectId hygiene.
Singleplayer auto-submission only fires when finalScore > 0 (line 70). This is fine but means a player who loses on round 1 never appears on the leaderboard — that may or may not be desired UX.
Leaderboard has no DELETE/cleanup endpoint, so accumulated TEST_/Anonymous Scholar entries will grow forever. Consider adding a TTL index or admin purge for non-seed entries older than N days.

rca of the issue: ROOT CAUSE: motor's insert_one() mutates the input dict in-place to attach the generated MongoDB _id (ObjectId). The endpoint then returned `{**doc}` — a shallow copy that still contained the ObjectId. FastAPI's jsonable_encoder cannot serialize ObjectId, raising TypeError: 'ObjectId' object is not iterable. REPRODUCTION: curl -X POST /api/leaderboard -d '{"name":"x","score":1}' returned HTTP 500. MITIGATION: doc.pop('_id', None) before returning. Long-term: use a Pydantic response_model with `model_config = {arbitrary_types_allowed: False}` and explicit fields, or project _id away.
